name: Ted Kennedy
summary: Edward M. Kennedy was a Democratic senator for 47 years who sponsored major health, civil rights, disability and immigration laws and pressed for universal health coverage and a higher minimum wage. He voted against the 2002 Iraq war authorisation, called for a moratorium on executions, and supported labour unions and abortion rights. He opposed school vouchers and Social Security privatisation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Introduced single-payer national health insurance bills in 1970 and 1979 and called universal coverage the cause of his life; in 2008 he called health care a fundamental right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted in 2007 to raise the federal minimum wage to $7.25 and made minimum wage speeches in the Senate that year.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: in 1980 he spoke of keeping the free enterprise system free in fact, while he backed government programmes such as national health insurance and public employment.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted in 2008 to raise the tax rate on income over $1 million and said he would close tax loopholes in 1980.

unions-good.rationale: Sponsored a card-check bill in 2009, voted to restrict employer interference in union organising in 2007, and was rated 100% by the AFL-CIO.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Said in 1980 he would tame monopoly, and voted in 2001 and 2002 for bans on corporate and union donations to campaigns.

cut-welfare.rationale: Opposed the 1995 welfare overhaul and the 1996 block grants, and called the 2006 welfare reform bill legislative child abuse.

state-harmful.rationale: Consistently argued for government programmes such as national health insurance and public employment, which rejects the view that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted for background checks at gun shows in 1999 and said he had spoken out for gun control.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the 1996 federal marriage definition and the 2006 constitutional ban on same-sex marriage, saying the ban would make gays and lesbians permanent second-class citizens.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposed banning partial-birth abortion except to save the mother's life, and warned in 1987 that women would be forced into back-alley abortions.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sponsored the Civil Rights Act of 2008, backed minority business set-asides in 1998, and signed the NAACP centennial resolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Voted for comprehensive immigration reform in 2007 with a guest worker programme and path to citizenship, and defended the 1965 Act's family unification.

free-trade.rationale: Mixed: voted for permanent normal trade relations with China and a Peru agreement, but against CAFTA, fast-track authority and several trade pacts.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted to cut oil use 40% by 2025 and to factor global warming into federal planning.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Spoke against the 2000 Republican bill to repeal the estate tax and voted against repeal in 2006 and against raising the exemption in 2008.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said in 1969 that American boys were too valuable to be sacrificed for a false sense of military pride.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Voted for a 10% set-aside for minority- and women-owned businesses and sponsored a disparate-impact bill, which assign rights by group.

positive-liberty.rationale: Argued that equal pay and opportunity, health care and welfare give people real means to use their freedom.

school-vouchers.rationale: Described as a steadfast opponent of school vouchers, opposed D.C. vouchers in 1997 and education savings accounts in 1998.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted for the 2009 $825 billion economic recovery package and opposed a balanced-budget constitutional amendment in 1997.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mixed: he spoke of the free enterprise system being free in fact, and also of economic protections for workers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Reintroduced the Equal Rights Amendment in 2007 and backed equal pay, citing women's wages at 77 cents on the dollar.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposed Robert Bork's nomination in 1987 for his view of segregated lunch counters, and opposed segregation.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Cited women earning about 77 cents per dollar of men's earnings in 2007 and sponsored the Equal Rights Amendment.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Consistently backed federal programmes such as health insurance, education and public employment, rejecting a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said in 1979 he wanted freedom for black and brown people as well as white, and sponsored the Equal Rights Amendment in 2007.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said in 1980 that the demands of the people were for better government, and that the President serves at the pleasure of the people.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said in 1980 that the poor have human needs and that health must not condemn people to poverty; opposed welfare cuts.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted in 2002 to enlarge NATO, the opposite of ending permanent alliances.

death-penalty.rationale: Called for a moratorium on executions in 2001 and opposed limiting death penalty appeals in 1996.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Said in 1983 that the best defence against nuclear war is arms control and then disarmament.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted in 2002 to enlarge NATO to include Eastern European countries.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Favoured taxing the wealthy at higher rates and voted to raise the top rate in 2008, which is the opposite of a flat tax.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said in 1980 he would tame monopoly and close tax loopholes.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Voted against restricting race-based federal contracting in 1995 and against repealing the 10% minority business set-aside in 1998, and opposed banning affirmative action hiring.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Sponsored the Employment Non-Discrimination Act, which bars employment discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Spent 47 years in the Senate and campaigned on public programmes; his record is the opposite of withdrawal.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Voted against Social Security reserve and lockbox proposals and against a 1998 amendment for personal retirement accounts, and criticised Bush's privatisation push.

single-official-language.rationale: Voted against declaring English the official language of the United States in 2007.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Sponsored the Civil Rights Act of 2008, which establishes discrimination based on disparate impact.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Voted against military aid to the Contra insurgents in the mid-1980s, including a 1984 Nicaragua amendment.

corporate-influence.rationale: Voted for banning soft money and corporate and union donations to campaigns in 2001 and 2002.

job-guarantee.rationale: Spoke in 1980 of increasing the government's commitment to full employment with public employment programmes when necessary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Signed the 2009 Employment Non-Discrimination Act, which covers gender identity, and backed the 2007 version.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Supported formal recognition of the Armenian Genocide in 2007.

family-wage.rationale: Pushed minimum wage increases to $7.25 and spoke of the minimum wage's role in working families' lives.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted against the 2002 Iraq war authorisation, saying war should be a last resort after reasonable alternatives are exhausted.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called in 1983 for an immediate, mutual and verifiable nuclear freeze, and voted for the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty in 1999.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Sponsored a card-check bill and voted to protect union organising, supporting wages set through collective bargaining.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Opposed a balanced-budget constitutional amendment in 1997, the kind of binding borrowing limit this statement describes.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Voted for the 1999 Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty and for a 1983 nuclear freeze; but also voted in 1999 to deploy national missile defence.

women-suffrage.rationale: Reintroduced the Equal Rights Amendment in 2007 and said the 1980 party should back ratification, noting the nation had founding mothers as well as founding fathers.

close-ties-china.rationale: Voted for permanent normal trade relations with China in 2000 and called Nixon's China opening a magnificent gesture.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Said in 2007 the Senate must root out bigotry and prejudice in the country, and argued discrimination remains the obstacle for disabled and minority citizens.

notes: Research was limited: the 1980 DNC speech full text, True Compass, the Congressional Record and congress.gov were not reachable through fetch, so most answers rest on OnTheIssues vote summaries (medium), Wikiquote quotations of his speeches and Wikipedia. S6 is a Wikiquote compilation of his own words, not the full speech texts. Nothing from the 1990 Immigration Act, NCLB, CHIP, the 1996 minimum wage, Kosovo or the FISA immunity vote was verified from a page opened in this session, so those statements are null. Individual Senate votes are taken from OnTheIssues and not checked against roll calls. No inferred answers were used.
